title: Release 0.2.1: the integration pathway — proxy passthrough fixes, mesh proxy, tester guide
body:
## What this is

The work Harry asked for on 2026-11-16: make Mesh ready to hand to testers with one solid integration pathway. Nothing here is merged, deployed or published; merging is the founder's call.

The gaps were found by driving the proxy with the real client libraries (official Anthropic and OpenAI SDKs in TypeScript and Python, and the Claude Code command-line tool) against a stand-in provider that records what reaches it.

## What was wrong (present in the live build `73dcdfe`)

- **Working calls were taken away.** Any POST other than `/v1/messages`, `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/responses` got Mesh's own 404: token counting, embeddings, batches, file uploads, deletes. An app that uses embeddings could not be pointed at Mesh.
- **A credential could go to the wrong provider.** Passthrough requests chose the provider from `x-api-key` alone. The current Anthropic SDK and a Claude subscription login send a bearer token, so their `GET /v1/models` went to the OpenAI upstream carrying an Anthropic credential.
- The query string (`?beta=true`, which Claude Code sends) was dropped.
- A request no lever changed was still re-serialised (`1.0` became `1`; integers past 2^53 lose digits).
- A body Mesh could not read was rejected by Mesh instead of the provider.
- A taken port printed `listen EADDRINUSE`.

## What changed

- `packages/sdk-js/src/proxy.ts`: everything Mesh does not reduce is forwarded unchanged to the right provider (all methods; large uploads streamed); query string kept; untouched requests sent as the client's own bytes; `GET /mesh/health`.
- `mesh proxy`: the same proxy and Theo as `mesh start`, for any app or agent, leaving Claude Code alone. In both command tables (developer entry and shipped runtime), with a test that fails if they drift.
- A taken port says whether Mesh is already running there or names a free port.
- `packages/cli/src/start-theo.test.ts`: the timing race that failed the first `v0.2.0` release run is fixed.
- `docs/site/start.md`: rebuilt around the one tool. `docs/pilot/TESTER-GUIDE.md`: what to hand a tester (draft, not sent).
- Version 0.2.1 for both packages; hosted runtime rebuilt at `8366ddc` (sha256 `745d05747e8ff82e5c8aa071d3b75db3d2a69dd71bb3e7b5b60d5e0ce76d3f37`).
- `docs/ops/release-0.2.0-runbook.md`: a dated 0.2.1 section, including why npm refused `v0.2.0`.

## How it was checked

- `corepack pnpm typecheck` clean; `corepack pnpm test` 994 passed (68 files). New: `packages/sdk-js/src/proxy-clients.test.ts`, 20 cases with the real SDKs and two distinct stand-in providers.
- Clean install of the rebuilt `docs/site/dist` into an empty home: `mesh 0.2.1 (build 8366ddc)`, `mesh verify` passes, `mesh proxy` answers its health check, the official Python SDKs (anthropic 2.8.0, openai 3.51.0) pass 9 of 9 calls configured only through `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` / `OPENAI_BASE_URL`.
- The real Claude Code command-line tool completes a turn through the proxy. On its 30 built-in tools the default levers remove only `$schema`.
- Not done: no real provider was called.

## To release (founder's steps)

1. Merge with a merge commit. The website then serves build `8366ddc`.
2. On npmjs.com, recreate the trusted publisher for both packages with **npm publish** ticked under Allowed actions (the `v0.2.0` run was refused with `OIDC permission denied for this action`).
3. Push tag `v0.2.1` from `main`. Do not re-run the `v0.2.0` release.

title: fix(core): the lossless tool-schema lever no longer deletes $defs (and rebuilds the hosted runtime)
body:
## What
The default-on `tool-schema-compaction` lever, which is labelled lossless, was corrupting some tool schemas. This fixes it and rebuilds the hosted runtime so the website ships the fix.

**Merging this deploys the website** (it changes `docs/site/dist`). Merging is the founder's step.

## The bug
Reproduced on `main` (`b52a3cf`) through `reduceRequest` with the three default levers, and on the live build `df70f3f`:

| Tool schema | What was sent to the provider |
|---|---|
| A nested model: `$ref: "#/$defs/Customer"` with a `$defs.Customer` (the shape Pydantic emits) | The `$ref` intact, `$defs` gone. The reference points at nothing |
| Parameters literally named `$id`, `$schema` or `$comment` | The parameters deleted, while `required` still listed them |
| `default`, `const`, `enum` or `examples` data containing `$id`, `$schema` or `$comment` keys | Those keys stripped from the data |

The first was reported on 2026-11-15; the other two were found while reproducing it and are the same fault: the lever treated names and data as schema keywords.

What a provider does with the dangling reference (reject the request, or accept it with the definition missing) was **not tested**; no real provider was called.

## The fix (`73dcdfe`, `packages/core/src/tool-schema.ts`)
- `$defs` is never removed, referenced or not.
- The keys of name-to-schema maps (`properties`, `patternProperties`, `$defs`, `definitions`, `dependentSchemas`, `dependencies`) are treated as names.
- Data values (`default`, `const`, `enum`, `examples`, `example`, `input_examples`) are copied through untouched.
- `$id` is kept on any tool that uses a reference keyword, since a reference may resolve against it.

Unchanged: `$schema`, `$comment`, `$id` on tools without references, and titles that only restate a property name are still removed.

### Why not prune unreferenced definitions (#38)
#8, #16 and #38 each propose a fix; #38 removes only definitions that no `$ref` reaches. Proving a definition unreferenced means resolving every form a `$ref` can take. #38 recognises `#/$defs/X` and `#/definitions/X` at the top level only, merges names across containers, and treats a parameter that is itself named `definitions` as a definitions container, so it can still delete something a reference needs. For a lever billed as unable to change the answer, keeping every definition is the safe rule. Pruning can come back later behind a quality gate. #8, #16 and #38 can be closed if this merges.

## Effect on savings
No recorded fixture or wire capture in the repo uses `$defs`, and no pinned figure moved (all number-pinning tests pass). `docs/NUMBERS.md` is unchanged. On schemas that do use `$defs`, the lever now saves less than it used to claim, because that saving came from deleting content.

## Hosted runtime
Rebuilt at `73dcdfe` (commit `1a70246`). Manifest: build `73dcdfe`, sha256 `0c75411453dcff5f1c9851a89c99eab9234029e8ae95ee2bde17b0e00c79090e`. Pages are unchanged. This is also the first hosted build made from a tree containing everything on `main`.

One request with a nested-model tool, sent through each built runtime to a stand-in provider:

| Build | Provider received `$defs` | Parameter `$id` | Schema identical to what the client sent |
|---|---|---|---|
| `df70f3f` (live) | no | no | no |
| `73dcdfe` (this PR) | yes | yes | yes |

## Checked (2026-11-16, macOS arm64, Node 24)
- 971 tests pass in 67 files at default timeouts (12 new); `tsc -b` and `typecheck:lab` clean.
- SDK package and its cold-install smoke test; CLI package and its two smoke tests.
- A clean-home install from the rebuilt site reports `mesh 0.2.0 (build 73dcdfe)` and `mesh verify` passes.
- Not checked: any real provider; the upgrade and rollback on this build; Linux and Windows locally (CI covers them).

## How to merge
Use **Create a merge commit**. Do not squash or rebase: the hosted runtime is stamped with commit `73dcdfe`, and either would remove that commit from `main`'s history.

After merging, wait for "Deploy site to GitHub Pages", then check `https://www.mesh-technology.com/mesh-version.json` shows `"version": "73dcdfe"`. Cut the `v0.2.0` npm tag only after that.

## Not changed
- `evals/fundamentals/value/a2_encoding_value.py` has its own copy of the old plumbing list. It is a research script, not product code.
